🚨In today's Speculator's Digest: "Blood in the Streets?"🩸🗡️📄🆓 the always sensible Lobo @DueDiligenceGuy Tiggre discusses how his "favorite minerals—except #uranium—took it on the chin" this past week💥🥊 which drove #mining #stocks lower for good reason—except in the case of uranium stocks:

🐺"Uranium stocks keep falling even though the metal itself is doing fine. I see this as an outstanding opportunity already—one that keeps getting more compelling."🎁⚛️⛏️🛒😊

Lobo also kindly reminds us that it can be difficult to predict when uranium stocks will bottom, as they can spike higher "at any moment" on a surprise catalyst or if Mr. Market suddenly recognizes this compelling opportunity.🤑

🐺"I’m glad I paused my recent move to buy uranium stocks. I’m looking forward to restarting as soon as the AI headwind subsides. But if share prices get too stupid-cheap to resist, I just might start buying anyway.   Why?  Because:
👉Other mining stocks are falling with their underlying minerals. But uranium is not falling. Mr. Market might realize that at any moment.
👉Uranium stocks often rebound sharply—not carving out a bottom, just shooting up again. I don’t want to miss that.
👉Uranium is recession-resistant. If everything else goes south, my uranium stocks might be my main saving grace.
👉Less solid, but still true, is that uranium stocks started selling off before everything else. Perhaps they will bottom before the others as well."

When Lobo says "Uranium is recession-resistant", I hope U understand that when economies go into a recession they will likely shut down a number of coal & gas-fired power plants if industry grinds to a halt and electricity demand slows, dropping demand for those fossil fuels, but #Nuclear power plants keep on running 24/7 and consuming uranium fuel regardless.⚛️⚡️🔌🏫🏥👮🚒🚑🏭🏢  In fact, it's "always on" Nuclear reactors that are relied on to keep schools, hospitals, emergency services and other essential industries operating to help economies power their way through a recessionary period.💪⚛️  Recessions won't generally lead to a reduction in uranium demand unless there is a deep economic depression with mass unemployment, in which case some reactors could be taken offline.😬

Anyway, I highly recommend subscribing to Lobo's free newsletter as it is always filled with common sense thoughts and ideas on how to be a successful investor in the resources sector.👍 Thanks for the words of wisdom, Lobo!🦉🙏🤠🐂
